pr_body:
The `group` key should take a normal string, not a more restrictive `uuid4_hex`. There are only 3 possible values for group ids anyway.

The original test for the code passes because it did not test the `CONFIG_SCHEMA`. The config fixture is partially built and group information is injected at runtime, bypassing the schema validation.

issue_context.title: Cannot use groups in trusted_users
issue_context.body:
### The problem

According to the [documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/authentication/providers/#trusted-users-examples) for the `trusted_networks` auth provider, one can use `group: group-name` for allowing a user group from trusted networks.

However such configuration will cause HA to start in safe mode with the following error message:

```
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.auth.providers] Invalid configuration for auth provider trusted_networks: Invalid Version4 UUID for dictionary value @ data['trusted_users']['192.168.0.0/24'][0]['group']. Got 'system-users'
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.config] Invalid config for [homeassistant]: Invalid Version4 UUID for dictionary value @ data['trusted_users']['192.168.0.0/24'][0]['group']. Got None. (See /config/configuration.yaml, line 1).
```

Looking at the [source code](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/auth/providers/trusted_networks.py#L49), the provider expects a `uuid4_hex` data type for group values, which is the same format as a user id. However groups in HA does not have a hex id, they are just plain text strings.

This should be a simple fix, just change `cv.uuid4_hex` to `str`.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.2.2
